data.one_liner: A Flutter library for explicit, implicit, and staggered animations using the Animator and AnimateWidget.
data.what_it_does: Provides simplified interfaces like Animator and AnimateWidget to separate animation setup from the UI. It supports implicit, explicit, and staggered animations without being constrained to dedicated AnimatedFoo widgets.
use_when: You want to perform implicit or explicit animations without needing dedicated AnimatedFoo widgets.
You need to implement complex staggered animations easily.
You want to separate animation setup logic from the user interface.
avoid_when: You prefer using low-level AnimationController and standard Flutter transition widgets exclusively.
You want a dedicated Rive or Lottie runtime package.
strengths: Simplifies both implicit and explicit animations under unified widgets.
Supports staggered animations and custom curves per animated value.
Allows control of animations from outside the widget using AnimatorKey.
weaknesses: Depends on the states_rebuilder library ecosystem.
Documentation outside of README examples is sparse.

alternatives.name: flutter_animate
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a comprehensive chainable extension-based animation system for Flutter widgets.

alternatives.name: animate_do
alternatives.why_pick_it: Offers ready-to-use entrance and attention animation widgets based on Animate.css.

data.minimal_example:
Center(
    child: AnimateWidget(
        duration: const Duration(seconds: 2),
        curve: Curves.fastOutSlowIn,
        builder: (context, animate) => Container(
            width: animate.call(100.0),
            height: animate(200.0, 'height'),
            color: animate(Colors.blue),
            child: const FlutterLogo(size: 75),
        ),
    ),
)
